# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 85 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 85 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_085_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Chapter 2

**1** Now the twelve virgins were carrying the stones and passing them through the gate and handing them to the young men, and the young men were fitting them into the tower. **2** Those who were not virgins were dragging stones up from the deep and carrying them; and the deep was on the left side of the gate, where the virgins were standing. **3** After all the stones had been fitted in, others were taken up from the deep. **4** These stones were brought up all around and fitted into the tower; they were quite smooth on all sides, fitting exactly with the other stones. **5** They were fitted together so well that their joints were invisible, and the tower appeared to be built from a single stone. **6** But other stones were brought up from the deep — some speckled, some rough, some white, some variegated — and all of these were fitted in by the young men. But many of these were carried away and thrown aside, and many were cast far from the tower by the virgins themselves and lay by the roadside. **7** But others that had been removed by them the builders put back against the stone from the deep from which they had been cut — yet they did not fit, for they were found unsuitable for the building. **8** And he said to me, "Do you see these stones?" "I see them, Lord," I replied. "These stones that are cast away," he said, "shall never enter the tower." **9** Some of the stones lying by the roadside were broken in two; some were cracked; some were chipped all around; some were completely shattered; and some remained whole — but most of them remained whole, awaiting that place.

---

### Translator's Note
The construction scene reveals the tower's dual source: stones passed through by the virgins (virtues) and stones hauled from the deep (baptismal candidates). The perfect jointure of v. 5 is a powerful image of ecclesiastical unity. The rejected stones represent baptized Christians who have sinned and are not yet incorporated, but most "remain whole" (v. 9) — awaiting the possibility of repentance and entry. SOPHIA follows LOGOS throughout.
